$comment: TUNED MATERIAL CONSTANTS for the dark-standard profile — C9a.
A real patch, not the identity: only one scheme's numbers can be the
runtime default, and the default is light-standard. An application in dark
mode applies this:
createGlassRoot({ materialProfile: patch })
Nothing selects it automatically yet. That is C9a's parent-impact item — the
runtime has no colour-scheme input to the material — and until it lands, dark
mode is correct only for a host that passes this itself.

cells. The dark profile captured six scenes, and its two solid-backdrop
scenes yield an empty native silhouette: over a flat backdrop of its own
tone the reference is within 0.02 linear luminance of it, which is a real
property of the material and not a capture fault, but it leaves no interior
to sample. Four cells is a thin basis and the numbers below are stated with
that thinness rather than around it.

$comment-provenance: THE PROVENANCE HOLE THIS CLOSES (2026-09-01, found by the landing review).
`capture-web.ts` hashes THIS FILE and writes the digest into every cell's
capturePath, so that a capture's optics can be reproduced from what the cell
records. But the optics are not this file: they are the renderer's
DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PROFILE with `patch` merged over it. A constant that moves in
the renderer's defaults and is not named here changes the rendered material
while leaving this file — and therefore the recorded SHA — untouched. Two
different materials then claim the same configuration, which is the exact
failure `capture-web.ts`'s own MATERIAL_PATCH_KEYS comment describes: plausible
numbers, wrong configuration, and no error anywhere.
`sizeOcclusionGain` did this. It was refitted 0 -> 0.05 against the frozen bed
(claims 5.26), the rendered material changed, and this file did not.
Two fixes, because they guard different things:
This profile's `patch` stays a DIFFERENCE document — it names what the dark
scheme retunes and nothing else, which is what makes the light profile's
identity claim meaningful. So fix (1) does not apply here; padding it with
constants identical to the default would destroy exactly the distinction the
file exists to draw.
`resolvedMaterialSha256` closes the hole for this profile instead: a digest over
the fully RESOLVED material (DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PROFILE + patch, keys sorted,
first 16 hex), recomputed by tuned-profiles.test.ts. It moves when the resolved
material moves, whatever moved it — including a renderer default this patch
deliberately declines to mention.

whatAnsweredTheCaveat: The caveat below says a lerp cannot hold the interior level and pass the
backdrop's structure at the same time, and it is right about a lerp that
has to carry the level. Under backdropToneResponseStrength 1 it does not:
the response law sets the level and the alpha is left carrying only the
passthrough, which is what the seven-point sweep above measures directly
(the body flat to 0.0002 across three of the swept alphas while pass moves
The multiply the caveat proposed is not needed, and the probe says so on
evidence rather than by argument: on the equal-mean pair, where the level
and the structure move independently, the lerp's prediction is closer on
three of the four components (claims 5.89 section 4). W21 Decision Log 2 (c)

caveat: 0.97 means very nearly opaque, and that is in tension with the reference's
own spread: it passes 7% to 13% of the backdrop's structure through, which
an alpha of 0.97 cannot do. The two observations are not reconcilable in
this renderer because its tint is a LERP toward a colour, and a lerp must
trade the interior level against the structure that survives it.
A MULTIPLY composite gets both, and the fixtures favour it. Inferring the
transmission from the spread ratio and from the mean separately, a multiply
model agrees with itself to within a factor of 1.3, 0.6, 1.2 and 0.5 on the
four cells; the lerp is off by three to nine times. That is evidence for a
hypothesis, not a proof — four cells at factor-two scatter — and it is
recorded as parent-impact rather than acted on, because a blend mode is a
new renderer parameter and not a tunable.

This is the one place the sweep found a large win and it was not taken.
The dark scheme is where the reference's rim is strongest and genuinely
measurable — peaks of 0.041 to 0.055, well clear of the code step at these
dark levels — and after the tint tune the rim becomes the dominant error

It was declined on three grounds. The residual bottoms out at almost exactly
the mean of the reference's own rim peaks, which means the win comes from
vitrea's rim going to ZERO rather than from it matching — removing a feature
the reference demonstrably has. The per-cell direction is not consistent:
on three cells vitrea's rim is too bright and on the fourth it is too dim
(0.0099 against 0.0478), so the mean is not describing a single error. And
the metric summarises the rim as a peak above the deepest ring's baseline,
which is not comparable across the very different opacities being compared
once the body is near-opaque.
Fitting a four-cell mean by deleting the feature it measures is fitting the
estimator. The gap is reported instead.
